title: Reduced-motion placement highlight is dropped entirely, contradicting the 'highlight steady' claim in three places
detail: The proc returns before drawing anything under reduced motion, yet the file header, the proc comment, and the PR body all promise a steady highlight (E9.2 'presence, not motion'). The placement feedback is silently absent.
recommended_fix: Draw the band at a fixed full alpha when v.reduced_motion (skip only the fade), or amend the PR body and both comments to state the highlight is disabled under reduced motion.

title: Reveal fades the type-chip hairline through DrawRectangleLinesEx — violating the diff's own rlsw line-alpha rule
evidence:
// the paper chip + ink hairline (full-alpha — the rlsw line-alpha trap)
-	out.a = 255
-	rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx({x0, y0, cw, ch}, max(1.0, s * 0.02), out)
+	out.a = u8(255 * fade)
+	rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx({x0, y0, cw, ch}, max(1.0, s * 0.02 * reveal_scale), out)
detail: During the reveal fade<1 feeds partial alpha into a LINE primitive. Per this diff's own repeated rule, the rlsw software renderer ignores line alpha, so golden captures render a solid hairline while the GPU app fades it.
recommended_fix: Keep out.a = 255 for the hairline (fade only the fills), or replace DrawRectangleLinesEx with thin filled quads so the fade survives the software renderer.

title: run_destroy deletes temp-arena shadow arrays — the same invalid-free pattern this PR removes from strict_spawn_class
evidence:
+	shadow := shadow_clone(state, context.temp_allocator)
+	defer pp.run_destroy(&shadow)
+	// TEMP allocator — the `defer delete`s were invalid frees (the temp arena
 	parent := make([]i32, n, context.temp_allocator)
-	defer delete(parent)
detail: shadow_clone allocates every shadow array from context.temp_allocator, then run_destroy deletes them — exactly the 'temp arena owns the memory' bad-free pattern the W2 fold eliminates. The clone test repeats it; bad-free counts are only quoted for core.
recommended_fix: Check app/render tracker output; clone with context.allocator so run_destroy is legitimate, or skip run_destroy for temp-allocated shadows, mirroring the W2 fold.

title: Unreachable dedup reset inside the lead > SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS early return
detail: predicted_window is only ever assigned while lead <= SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS for that same window; the reset sits behind lead > SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS, so predicted_window == window can never hold there. Unreachable by construction.
recommended_fix: Delete the dead reset block, or implement the intended rollover where the telegraph timeline actually expires.

title: spawn_fx_init and spawn_fx_destroy are never called — only spawn_fx_reset is wired
detail: No call site exists for either proc; the app and harness only call spawn_fx_reset, so reveals grows from nil via append and the capacity-4 pre-allocation plus cleanup never run.
recommended_fix: Wire spawn_fx_init/spawn_fx_destroy into the View lifecycle, or delete both procs and rely on append-from-nil plus the per-run reset.

title: Dem comment misstates the t82 reveal envelope (~0.75/~0.8 vs actual ~0.49/~0.41)
evidence:
+#   4100 ms (t82)  — reveal mid-envelope (scale ~0.75, fade ~0.8)
+		k := f32(tick - r.spawn_tick) / f32(SPAWN_REVEAL_TICKS)
+		e := smoothstep01(k)
+		return 0.4 + 0.6 * e, 0.3 + 0.7 * e, true
detail: At t82 the reveal age is 2 of 8 ticks: k=0.25, smoothstep 0.156, giving scale ~0.49 and fade ~0.41 — not the quoted '~0.75, ~0.8', which matches roughly t85.
recommended_fix: Correct the 4100ms comment to scale ~0.49 / fade ~0.41, or move that capture to 4400ms if the quoted envelope was the intent.

title: Test comment says '2 tiles from the fixture router' — (13,10) to (12,10) is 1 tile
evidence:
+	// negative"): an OUT-OF-SEPARATION pending place (2 tiles from the
+	// fixture router - below the 4-tile router_router floor) is rejected by
+	pp.topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, rt, {12, 10}, cat)    // id 1
+	bad := []pp.Command{{kind = pp.Cmd_Place_Router{type_idx = rt_idx, pos = {13, 10}}, apply_tick = 77}}
detail: The bad place (13,10) is 1 tile from the fixture router at (12,10), not 2; the assertion message '(2 < 4)' repeats the error. The rejection conclusion still holds either way.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment and assert message to say 1 tile, or move the bad place to a genuine 2-tile offset if that was intended.

title: Ring table copied per segment inside the draw loop
evidence:
+	for i in 0 ..< SPAWN_RING_SEGS {
+		table := SPAWN_RING_TABLE // local copy — a constant can't be indexed by a runtime index
detail: The 36x2 f32 table is copied inside the per-segment loop — 36 copies per annulus, two annuli per ring, every frame in the raster path. One hoisted copy per call suffices.
recommended_fix: Hoist 'table := SPAWN_RING_TABLE' above the for loop; the runtime-index workaround needs only a single stack copy per call.
